posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Well I discovered for myself what happens to a 1.25% TEA solution left in a tightly stoppered (air removed) bottle in a cabinet for three months.

It still goes bad.

When your TEA smells a bit like a fish tank that needs cleaning, it's time to throw it out.

How many of you keep your TEA solutions past one use? Do you refrigerate or just replace it more often than every couple or three uses?

posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md:
yes, i discovered this, too. the tea solution ( any concentrations, I think) get's bad after a few months. there are mostly flakes of mould in it, it seems. 

But you can put it through a filter to get out the flakes and reuse it. the smelling is no problem. as you wash your holograms anyway it's no problem. for swelling the solution works although it is a little bit smelling. I use my tea solution over one year now. I only had to filter it sometimes.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md: I also typically use it until I see floaters (about a month around here). In this case the TEA was clear but had an oh so unpleasant smell.

posts.author: jeff-blyth
posts.content_md:
> **MichaelH:** I also typically use it until I see floaters (about a month around here). In this case the TEA was clear but had an oh so unpleasant smell.

Your observation is interesting Michael and suggests to me that on your side of the pond you have particularly adept bacteria or moulds at breaking down this amine and removing I guess the OH group which has been making the chemical not very smelly. So that means it is probably forming the much more smelly triethylamine . As HoloM suggests in this thread, this pongy TEA is no big deal on the holography side and works just as well as the fresh stuff apparently. 

Fact is we have actually evolved from our ape or possibly pre-ape past millions of years ago to not like the smell of volatile amines because they were given off by rotting meat, ( same for hydrogen sulfide gas too.) So any ancestral forms of pre-humans who found the smell unpleasant were selected for, leaving behind those protohumans who ignored it to die early from botulism, and general food-poison nasties. 

Meanwhile of course blow-flies had long earlier evolved the mechanism to luxuriate in rotting meat as do kommodo dragons and vultures.

Anyway back to the holography lab. My bottles of TEA/water solutions have kept for years and have not gone off pong wise, according to my young colleagues whose noses have not undergone 50 years worth of various chemical assaults like mine has.

So perhaps the organisms dont thrive in the British climate so well.

jeff

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
I'd guess that your lab is probably more sterile than mine? Perhaps also better temperature controlled?

Being in a house I get a lot of dust and such that I try to keep down but my chemicals are stored in bathroom cabinets and this particular bathroom is on the west side of the house and the temperature does fluctuate a fair amount during the course of the day. I haven't tracked it but this room definitely goes from "cool" to "fairly warm" toward the end of the day.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: I always threw my diluted TEA solutions out at the end of the day. I found this necessary to keep the concentration constant (because of water evaporation) and therefore the final color of the holograms as desired. TEA is cheap ... tossing a 12x16" plate because it's the wrong color is expensive!

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: Funny - I re-use TEA solutions for months and months and have never seen this. They do eventually build up a bit of chemicalish smell which I attribute to soaking out preservatives from emulsions... Maybe the film preservatives are preserving the TEA mix? I also store the mixes at fairly low temperature - 10 to 15C.
